answer: Coordination Clock Auction. Each identity must win a timed slot to broadcast, with slots auctioned per dawn and priced by the number of simultaneous bidders. Winners get a signed wharf token valid only for that window; messages outside a held slot are dropped. A juniper-scented nonce is embedded per slot and checked by relayers, so replaying one identity across slots requires winning each auction separately. An attacker running N sybils pays N times the clearing price every cycle, making sustained coordination cost linear in identities rather than amortized.
